title: Play Now - Zombie Slayer
author: Futuristocrat
selftext:
Hi everyone!  
I've been working on an arcade first-person-shooter game called Zombie Slayer.

Play it here: [Play Zombie Slayer](https://idontknowwhatiamdoingthough.github.io/Zombie-Slayer---Game/)

It was entirely built using Gemini in Antigravity. 

A few things that makes this game awesome:

\- Only 2 MB in size and it’s a single HTML file.  
\- Runs directly in your browser, no download or installation required.  
\- Built by someone who had no programming experience (still don’t).  
\- Created entirely through hundreds of AI prompts over months of work.  
\- The world, gameplay, and even the sound effects are procedurally generated.

I felt like an art director rather than a programmer - it is my vision, art style, and ideas, AI just developed my vision. Even with AI doing the coding, it still took a huge amount of time, experimentation, and refinement.

I had a blast making it. My plan is to keep improving the game over time - keeping up with the latest AI models to see what this can turn into. In theory, this game would expand exponentially as AI improves. 

I'd really appreciate any feedback - whether it's gameplay, balance, bugs, or ideas for new features.

Thanks for giving it a try!

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body: Great work! Are you going to generate custom 3D assets for it, or is it meant to have that voxel look?

replies.author: Futuristocrat
replies.body: Thank you! That voxel look is a byproduct of how the game was built - it is entirely procedurally generated, every rectangular prism is a line of code. This allowed me to avoid using programs outside of the coding interface (Google’s Antigravity) and kept the game to a single self contained 2MB HTML file. I want to keep it to these restrictions, since that’s what makes this game unique. What bothers me the most is how Minecraft-like the zombies look, which I’ll fix in a future update.

comments.author: TradeNPlayz
comments.body: Gameplay looks decent, but music really needs some work.

replies.author: Futuristocrat
replies.body: Haha fair enough. I agree that the music needs some more love. Better audio is on the long list of improvements I want to make.
